answers.value: All in-force property exposures on the current bound book across personal and commercial property, flood WYO and specialty programs; scope = every location record with a street address in Guidewire PolicyCenter that lacks validated lat/long, run before each quarterly CAT accumulation cycle.
The in-force snapshot as of the quarter-end accumulation date (e.g. 2026-06-30); only policies in-force on that date are geocoded, plus new/endorsed locations bound since the prior snapshot.

Each location has full street address, city, state, ZIP and country populated; geocoder returns lat/long with a match-level code. Records geocoded only to ZIP-centroid (match level < parcel/rooftop) are flagged for manual review; missing state or ZIP rejects the record.

Count of geocoded locations reconciles to the in-force location count in PolicyCenter (delta = 0); total insured value (TIV) of geocoded locations reconciles to the in-force TIV within 0.5%; any variance investigated before the file is released to Moody's RMS.

Geocoded exposure extract saved to SharePoint /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/geocoding/ as geocode_result_v<n>.csv with run timestamp, geocoder version and match-rate summary; retained 7 years per accumulation audit trail.

Locations that fail to geocode above ZIP-centroid logged in the geocoding exception register with disposition (manual-coordinate / hold-from-model / accept-ZIP-centroid) and analyst initials; unresolved exceptions above 2% of TIV escalated to the Exposure Management Manager.

checklist.step: Apply address and geocode data-quality rules for the exposure domain
checklist.value: Location domain rules enforce non-null state/ZIP and require a geocoder match-level code before a record is admitted to the CAT model feed.

checklist.step: Quarantine records below rooftop/parcel match quality
checklist.value: Records geocoded only to ZIP-centroid are routed to the manual-review queue rather than passed straight to RMS.

testing.step: Measure geocode match rate against threshold
testing.value: Rooftop/parcel match rate ≥ 95% of TIV; any quarter below threshold triggers a data-quality corrective action.

testing.step: Sample failed records for correct disposition
testing.value: Sample 25 quarantined locations; 100% show a recorded disposition and, where accepted, documented rationale.

checklist.step: Validate the exposure extract before model ingestion
checklist.value: Automated validation confirms TIV, location count and coordinate ranges are within expected bounds versus the prior snapshot.

testing.step: Reconcile geocoded TIV to source-of-record

answers.value: Aggregate in-force TIV and modeled loss by CRESTA/CAT zone against the board-approved zonal capacity limits and the reinsurance program per-occurrence and per-zone retentions; scope = all catastrophe-exposed property zones (US wind, quake, flood, SCS).

Monitored continuously against the current in-force book, refreshed at each quarter-end accumulation run (e.g. Q2 2026 as of 2026-06-30) and re-checked intra-quarter on any large single-risk bind that could move a peak zone.

Each zone row carries current aggregate TIV, modeled 1-in-100 and 1-in-250 loss, approved limit, headroom and utilisation %. Rows missing an approved limit or a current modeled loss are treated as invalid and excluded from the breach calculation until corrected.

Sum of zonal aggregates reconciles to the total in-force accumulation report (delta = 0); the utilisation calculation ties limit and exposure to the CAT Authority Matrix v3.1 capacity table; any unreconciled zone is held from sign-off.

Zonal utilisation dashboard and breach list exported to /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/zonal-monitoring/ as zonal_utilisation_v<n>.xlsx with timestamp and RMS event-set version; retained 7 years.

Zones exceeding 90% utilisation flagged amber and >100% flagged red in the breach register with disposition (buy fac reinsurance / restrict binding / accept with CUO waiver); red breaches escalate same day to the Exposure Management Manager and CUO.
All catastrophe-exposed zones in the current accumulation run (census); every zone is tested for its utilisation against the approved limit, not a sample.

PASS = every zone at or below 100% of approved limit, or any overage covered by a documented CUO waiver or in-force facultative cession. FAIL = any zone over limit without a waiver or offsetting cover.

On a red breach, open a capacity-exception item, notify the Exposure Management Manager, and pursue mitigation (facultative purchase, binding restriction, or non-renewal plan) with a resolution target of 10 business days; re-run the accumulation after mitigation.
Acceptance = zonal utilisation report produced for 100% of zones, all breaches dispositioned, and headroom recalculated after any mitigation, signed by the Exposure Management Manager.

Evidence (utilisation report, breach register, waiver approvals) stored in /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/zonal-monitoring/ and linked from the quarterly accumulation governance pack.

checklist.step: Compare each zone's aggregate against its approved concentration limit
checklist.value: Utilisation = current aggregate / approved zonal limit computed per zone against the CAT Authority Matrix v3.1 capacity table.

checklist.step: Flag zones breaching or approaching the concentration limit
checklist.value: Amber at ≥90% and red at >100% utilisation, surfaced on the zonal dashboard each accumulation run.

testing.step: Verify no undocumented over-limit zone
testing.value: 0 zones over 100% utilisation without a CUO waiver or offsetting facultative cover.

checklist.step: Track aggregate exposure by peril and zone each cycle
checklist.value: Aggregate TIV and modeled loss tracked per CRESTA/CAT zone and reconciled to the total in-force accumulation.

testing.step: Reconcile zonal aggregates to the total book
testing.value: Sum of zonal aggregates equals the total in-force accumulation (delta = 0) for the tested quarter.

checklist.step: Route capacity overages to CUO for approval
checklist.value: Any bind that would push a zone over its approved limit is referred for CUO approval with documented rationale before it is retained.

testing.step: Confirm over-limit retentions carry CUO approval
testing.value: 100% of over-limit positions retained in the quarter have a documented CUO waiver on file.

answers.value: CRESTA-zone accumulation reports summarising aggregate TIV and modeled loss by CRESTA zone for internal governance (Risk Committee) and for reinsurer submission at renewal; scope = all catastrophe-exposed property in the in-force book grouped to CRESTA zones.
Produced at each quarter-end accumulation date (e.g. 2026-06-30) for internal governance, and as at the reinsurance renewal snapshot date for reinsurer reporting.

Each CRESTA row carries zone code, aggregate TIV, policy/location count and modeled 1-in-100/1-in-250 loss. Reports missing a CRESTA mapping for any location, or with unmapped 'zone 99' residual above tolerance, are not issued until the mapping gap is closed.

Total TIV across CRESTA zones reconciles to the in-force accumulation control total (delta = 0); location counts reconcile to the geocoded exposure file; residual/unmapped TIV kept below 0.5% or explained in a footnote.

Issued report (PDF plus data workbook) stored in /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/cresta-reports/ as cresta_accumulation_v<n> with timestamp, RMS event-set version and distribution list; retained 7 years.

Data or mapping issues found during production logged in the report exception log with disposition (remap / restate / footnote); any restatement after distribution is versioned and re-issued with a change note to recipients.
The full set of CRESTA zones in the accumulation run for the reported snapshot; all zones and the residual bucket are inspected before issue.
PASS = report ties to control totals, residual unmapped TIV < 0.5%, and all peril views (wind/quake/flood) present. FAIL = control-total break, residual over tolerance, or a missing peril view.

On a failed inspection, hold distribution, correct the mapping or extract, re-run, and re-inspect; material corrections found post-issue are re-issued as a versioned restatement within 5 business days.
Field definitions sourced from the accumulation data dictionary: cresta_zone, peril, aggregate_tiv, location_count, modeled_loss_100yr, modeled_loss_250yr — one row per zone per peril.

Source control totals: in-force TIV and location count from Guidewire PolicyCenter as of the snapshot date, and modeled-loss totals from the Moody's RMS run of record; both stamped on the report cover sheet.

Acceptance criteria: report ties to control totals, residual unmapped TIV < 0.5%, and all peril views present, signed by the Exposure Management Manager. Evidence (issued PDF, data workbook, reconciliation) stored in /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/cresta-reports/ and linked from the accumulation governance pack.

checklist.step: Aggregate exposure to CRESTA zones each reporting cycle
checklist.value: TIV and modeled loss aggregated per CRESTA zone and reconciled to the in-force accumulation control totals before issue.

testing.step: Reconcile the CRESTA report to source totals
testing.value: Report TIV ties to PolicyCenter in-force TIV and RMS modeled-loss totals with 0 unexplained variance.

checklist.step: Show zonal aggregates against concentration limits in the report
checklist.value: Each CRESTA zone reported alongside its approved concentration limit and utilisation for governance visibility.

testing.step: Verify limit context is present for peak zones
testing.value: 100% of peak zones in the report show the approved limit and current utilisation.

answers.value: Underwriting-action recommendations to relieve concentration peaks in over-utilised CAT zones — e.g. binding moratoria, sub-limit tightening, non-renewal targeting, facultative purchase or geographic re-mix; scope = the amber/red zones identified in the current accumulation run.
Prepared each quarter for the zones breaching capacity in that accumulation cycle (e.g. Q2 2026), with recommendations effective from the next binding period until the peak is relieved.

Each recommendation names the target zone, current utilisation, the action, the estimated TIV/loss relief, and the affected LOB/segment. Recommendations without a quantified relief estimate or a named action owner are returned for completion.

The modeled post-action utilisation is recomputed and reconciled: projected relief per action sums to the reduction needed to bring the zone to or below its approved limit; residual overage after all actions is stated explicitly.

Recommendation memo and supporting relief model saved to /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/peak-actions/ as peak_relief_recommendation_v<n> with timestamp and the accumulation run reference; retained 7 years.

Where a peak cannot be relieved within appetite by underwriting action alone, the residual is logged as an exception with disposition (buy additional reinsurance / accept with CUO waiver / portfolio exit plan) and escalated to the Exposure Management Manager.

checklist.step: Target actions at zones over the concentration limit
checklist.value: Recommendations are generated for every zone above its approved concentration limit and sized to close the utilisation gap.

testing.step: Verify projected relief closes each peak
testing.value: For each over-limit zone, the sum of recommended actions brings modeled utilisation to ≤100% or the residual is explicitly dispositioned.

checklist.step: Align recommendations with the documented CAT appetite
checklist.value: Actions reference the CAT Risk Appetite Statement FY26 for the affected LOB, geography and industry so the re-mix stays within appetite.

testing.step: Confirm recommendations respect appetite bounds
testing.value: 0 recommended actions push another zone or segment outside its documented appetite band.

checklist.step: Escalate un-relievable peaks for CUO decision
checklist.value: Residual overages that cannot be closed by underwriting action are packaged for CUO approval with quantified retained risk.

testing.step: Confirm residual peaks carry a documented decision
testing.value: 100% of residual over-limit positions have a CUO waiver or an approved mitigation plan on file.

Recipients documented on the distribution list: Chief Underwriting Officer, Chief Risk Officer, Head of Reinsurance and Risk Management Committee members; distribution logged with send date and version.
All quarterly CAT-exposure reports issued in the period under review; each is traced from source accumulation run through to the committee minutes.

Effective date = the quarter-end accumulation snapshot (e.g. 2026-06-30); the report reflects the in-force position and reinsurance program in effect on that date, and is valid for that quarter's governance cycle only.

answers.value: Catastrophe model runs on the in-force exposure set using Moody's RMS (with AIR as challenger) to produce PML and TVaR by peril and return period; scope = all cat-exposed property, run gross and net of the reinsurance program.
Run on the quarter-end accumulation snapshot (e.g. 2026-06-30) and re-run at reinsurance renewal and after any model/event-set version change during the year.

The exposure import passes RMS data-completeness checks (geocode match, construction/occupancy/year-built coded, TIV present); unmapped or defaulted characteristics are quantified. A run with import warnings above the defaulting tolerance is not used for reporting.

Imported TIV and location count reconcile to the geocoded exposure feed (delta = 0); modeled loss totals reconcile to the prior run within an explained movement corridor; secondary-uncertainty and demand-surge settings match the approved run configuration.

Run outputs (EP curves, PML/TVaR by peril, run log) exported to /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/model-runs/ as rms_run_v<n> with RMS software and event-set version, analysis settings and timestamp; retained 7 years.

Import defaults, geocode gaps or setting deviations logged in the model-run exception register with disposition (accept / rerun after fix); deviations from the approved configuration require Exposure Management Manager approval before the run is designated run of record.

RMS software version and event-set (e.g. NA Hurricane v23) are on the approved-vendor-model register; the blending approach between RMS and AIR is the current Board-approved methodology documented in the CAT model governance file.
Sensitivity thresholds: a >10% movement in 1-in-100 PML versus the prior run, or a >15% divergence between RMS and AIR, triggers a documented reasonableness review before the run is accepted.
Materiality threshold: any peril whose net 1-in-250 loss exceeds 5% of capital, or moves the reinsurance sufficiency conclusion, is flagged as material and reviewed with the Capital Model Actuary.
The full in-force exposure set for the snapshot; the run is re-performed end-to-end on the same exposure import to confirm reproducibility, not a sample.

PASS = re-run reproduces PML/TVaR within 0.1% on identical inputs and settings, and all model/version/setting parameters match the approved configuration. FAIL = non-reproducible output or an unapproved setting.

A non-reproducible or out-of-corridor result is quarantined, root-caused (data, setting, or version), corrected, and re-run; the accepted run is re-designated run of record only after Exposure Management Manager sign-off, target 10 business days.
Approved methodology = the Board-approved RMS/AIR blending and secondary-uncertainty configuration recorded in the CAT model governance file, version-controlled with an effective date.

Parameters (event set, demand surge, secondary uncertainty, reinsurance structure) sourced from the approved run configuration and the ceded reinsurance system; each parameter's source is logged in the run log.

checklist.step: Produce PML across defined return periods
checklist.value: PML computed at 1-in-100 and 1-in-250 (and TVaR) by peril, gross and net of reinsurance, from the run of record.

testing.step: Verify PML reproducibility
testing.value: Re-running identical inputs reproduces PML within 0.1%; deviations are investigated before acceptance.

checklist.step: Use only approved vendor model versions
checklist.value: RMS software and event-set versions used are on the approved-vendor-model register with a recorded approval date.

testing.step: Confirm model version approval
testing.value: 100% of runs of record cite an approved model/event-set version; unapproved versions are rejected for reporting.

checklist.step: Compare results against the challenger model
checklist.value: Each cycle compares RMS PML/TVaR against AIR and documents the divergence and blending rationale.

testing.step: Verify divergence is within tolerance or explained
testing.value: RMS-vs-AIR divergence beyond 15% carries a documented reasonableness explanation.

answers.value: CAT sub-limits and per-risk and per-occurrence limits set by zone and peril so retained exposure aligns with the catastrophe reinsurance program's attachment, limit and reinstatements; scope = all cat-exposed zones and the per-risk limit grid used by underwriting.

Set at reinsurance program inception/renewal (e.g. effective 2026-07-01) and reviewed at each quarter-end accumulation cycle; limits remain in force for the treaty year unless a mid-term restructure occurs.

Each limit row carries zone, peril, per-risk limit, per-occurrence sub-limit and the mapped treaty layer. Rows without a mapped reinsurance layer or that exceed treaty capacity are rejected until reconciled to the program structure.

Aggregate of per-occurrence sub-limits reconciles to net retained occurrence exposure below the reinsurance attachment; the limit grid ties to the treaty schedule in the ceded system; any limit exceeding program capacity is held from activation.

Approved limit schedule stored in /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/cat-limits/ as cat_limit_schedule_v<n> with effective date, treaty-year reference and approval record; retained 7 years, and loaded to PolicyCenter/underwriting workstation as binding controls.

Proposed limits above program capacity or outside appetite are logged as exceptions with disposition (reduce limit / buy additional cover / CUO waiver); exceptions require CUO approval before the limit is activated.
The full CAT limit grid for the treaty year (all zone/peril combinations); every limit is traced back to the reinsurance program schedule as the source of record.

PASS = every per-occurrence sub-limit sits within the program's occurrence limit and each per-risk limit maps to a valid treaty layer. FAIL = any limit exceeding treaty capacity or without a mapped layer.

A limit that breaches program capacity is corrected (reduced or backed by additional facultative/treaty cover) or escalated for a CUO waiver before it is loaded as a binding control; target resolution 10 business days.

Acceptance = limit schedule approved, every row reconciled to the reinsurance program, and binding controls loaded to the policy and underwriting systems, signed off by the Exposure Management Manager.

Evidence (approved limit schedule, reconciliation to treaty schedule, system-load confirmation) stored in /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/cat-limits/ and linked from the renewal governance pack.

checklist.step: Set zonal and per-risk limits to enforce concentration limits
checklist.value: Per-occurrence sub-limits and per-risk limits are calibrated so retained zonal accumulation stays within the approved concentration limits.

testing.step: Verify limits keep zones within concentration bounds

checklist.step: Encode limits into the underwriting authority framework
checklist.value: Per-risk and per-occurrence limits are loaded as binding controls tied to authority levels in the CAT Authority Matrix v3.1.

testing.step: Confirm binding controls enforce the limits
testing.value: System binding controls reject risks exceeding the loaded per-risk limit without a referral.

checklist.step: Reconcile limits to tracked aggregate and the reinsurance program
checklist.value: The limit schedule reconciles to net retained aggregate below attachment and to the treaty schedule.

testing.step: Verify limit-to-program reconciliation
testing.value: 0 limits exceed reinsurance program capacity; every row maps to a valid treaty layer.

answers.value: Location-data quality validation for in-force exposures before CAT modeling: address completeness, geocode match level, and coding of construction, occupancy, year built, number of storeys and TIV; scope = all cat-exposed locations in the current in-force snapshot.
Validated on the quarter-end accumulation snapshot (e.g. 2026-06-30) and on incremental new/endorsed locations bound since the prior snapshot, ahead of each model run.

Required fields: full address, lat/long with match level, construction class, occupancy, year built and TIV. Locations with missing primary characteristics, ZIP-centroid-only geocodes, or TIV outside plausible bounds are flagged; default-coded characteristics above the tolerance % are reported.

Validated location count and TIV reconcile to the in-force book in PolicyCenter (delta = 0); the share of defaulted/unknown characteristics is measured against the prior snapshot to detect data drift.

Validation report (rule results, pass rate, defect list) saved to /Exposure-Management/CAT-Accumulation/<YYYY-Qn>/data-validation/ as location_validation_v<n> with timestamp and rule-set version; retained 7 years.

Failed locations logged in the data-quality exception register with disposition (correct at source / re-geocode / accept default with note); repeated coverholder or source-system defects are raised to the data owner and Exposure Management Manager for upstream fix.

checklist.step: Apply location data-quality rules before modeling
checklist.value: Rule set enforces completeness and validity for address, geocode match level, construction/occupancy/year-built and TIV on the exposure domain.

testing.step: Publish and check the data-quality score
testing.value: Location data-quality score ≥ the agreed threshold; sub-threshold snapshots trigger a corrective action before model use.

checklist.step: Document known data limitations for the run
checklist.value: Defaulted or unknown characteristics are quantified and documented so downstream modeling accounts for the uncertainty.

testing.step: Verify reconciliation and defect closure
testing.value: Validated TIV/count ties to source (delta = 0) and every high-severity defect is dispositioned before the exposure feed is released.

answers.value: Aggregate delegated-authority exposure across all active coverholders and binding authorities: bound premium, TIV and aggregate limits by coverholder, class and geography; scope = every open binder/coverholder reporting bordereaux into the delegated authority book.
Compiled monthly on receipt of coverholder bordereaux and consolidated at quarter-end (e.g. 2026-06-30) to align with the aggregate accumulation and reserving cycle.

Each coverholder row carries binder reference, reporting period, bound premium, TIV, aggregate limit used and number of risks. Rows with a missing or late bordereaux, or premium/limit outside the binder terms, are flagged and excluded from the aggregate until resolved.

Sum of coverholder-level premium and TIV reconciles to the consolidated aggregate control totals (delta = 0); bordereaux received count reconciles to the expected count of active binders; missing bordereaux quantified as a completeness gap.

Aggregate exposure workbook saved to /Delegated-Authority/Aggregate-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/aggregate-exposure/ as delegated_aggregate_v<n> with timestamp, bordereaux cut-off date and source-binder list; retained 7 years.

Late or non-conforming bordereaux logged in the coverholder exception register with disposition (chase / estimate with accrual / suspend binder); persistent breaches escalated to the Delegated Authority Manager and reflected in coverholder performance reviews.
All active coverholders/binders expected to report in the period (census); every expected bordereaux is checked in, not a sample.

PASS = 100% of expected bordereaux received and reconciled, aggregate ties to control totals, and no binder over its aggregate limit. FAIL = a missing bordereaux without an accrual, a control-total break, or a binder over aggregate.

A missing or broken bordereaux is chased against the binder reporting SLA; if unresolved, an estimated accrual is booked and the binder flagged for suspension review; exceptions tracked to closure within 10 business days.
Acceptance = consolidated aggregate reconciled to control totals, completeness gap quantified and dispositioned, and the compiled exposure signed off by the Delegated Authority Manager.
Evidence (aggregate workbook, bordereaux receipt log, exception register) stored in /Delegated-Authority/Aggregate-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/aggregate-exposure/ and linked from the DA oversight pack.

checklist.step: Track delegated aggregate exposure across coverholders
checklist.value: Premium, TIV and aggregate-limit usage tracked by coverholder and consolidated to the delegated book each cycle.

testing.step: Reconcile the delegated aggregate to control totals
testing.value: Consolidated premium/TIV ties to control totals with 0 unexplained variance and 100% expected-bordereaux completeness.

checklist.step: Apply bordereaux data-quality rules on intake
checklist.value: Each bordereaux is validated for required fields and binder-term conformance before it is admitted to the aggregate.

testing.step: Verify non-conforming rows are excluded
testing.value: 0 non-conforming bordereaux rows are included in the aggregate without a documented disposition.

answers.value: Assessment of geographic and class concentration within delegated-authority portfolios against company guidelines and the delegated appetite: exposure by CRESTA zone, class of business and coverholder versus documented concentration thresholds; scope = the consolidated delegated book.
Assessed quarterly on the consolidated aggregate as of quarter-end (e.g. 2026-06-30), and on any binder whose in-quarter growth materially shifts a zone or class concentration.

Each concentration row carries zone/class, aggregate exposure, the guideline threshold and utilisation %. Rows lacking a mapped guideline threshold, or with unclassified class-of-business, are flagged and resolved before the assessment is finalised.

Concentration aggregates reconcile to the consolidated delegated aggregate exposure (delta = 0); class and zone totals tie to the bordereaux data; residual unclassified exposure kept below 1% or explained.

Concentration assessment saved to /Delegated-Authority/Aggregate-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/concentration/ as delegated_concentration_v<n> with timestamp, threshold-set version and source-aggregate reference; retained 7 years.

Zones/classes over the guideline threshold logged in the concentration exception register with disposition (restrict binder / reduce aggregate limit / accept with DA Manager approval); breaches escalated to the Delegated Authority Manager.
Concentration methodology (zone/class definitions and threshold set) is the current company-approved delegated authority guideline version recorded in the DA governance file.
Sensitivity: a >10% quarter-over-quarter increase in any zone or class concentration triggers a documented review even if still under threshold.
Materiality: any single zone or class above 90% of its guideline threshold, or contributing >10% of delegated aggregate, is treated as material and reviewed with the Exposure Management Manager.
All zone and class-of-business combinations in the consolidated delegated book (census); every combination is assessed against its guideline threshold.
PASS = every zone/class at or below its guideline threshold, or any overage documented and approved. FAIL = any concentration over threshold without a recorded disposition.
On a breach, propose a binder restriction or aggregate-limit reduction, or record DA Manager approval to accept; track the mitigation to effect within 10 business days and re-assess after action.
Acceptance = concentration assessed for all zones/classes, breaches dispositioned, and the assessment signed off by the Delegated Authority Manager.
Evidence (concentration assessment, breach register, approvals) stored in /Delegated-Authority/Aggregate-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/concentration/ and linked from the DA oversight pack.

Approved methodology = the company-approved delegated concentration guideline (zone/class definitions and thresholds) recorded in the DA governance file; parameters (thresholds, appetite bands) sourced from that guideline version with an effective date logged in the assessment.

checklist.step: Assess delegated concentration against limits
checklist.value: Zone and class concentrations in the delegated book are measured against documented concentration limits/guidelines each quarter.

testing.step: Verify no undocumented concentration breach
testing.value: 0 zone/class concentrations over threshold without a recorded disposition or approval.

checklist.value: Concentration outcomes feed ongoing coverholder monitoring so binders driving over-appetite build-up are reviewed and restricted.

testing.step: Confirm monitoring actions on breaching binders
testing.value: Every coverholder contributing to a concentration breach has a monitoring action (restriction/review) recorded.

answers.value: Consolidation of all coverholder bordereaux (risk and premium) into the aggregate delegated book for the reporting period; scope = every bordereaux submitted by active coverholders/binders for the month, mapped to the company data model.
Consolidated monthly on the bordereaux reporting cut-off (e.g. bordereaux for period ending 2026-06-30 received by the binder SLA date) and rolled into the quarter-end aggregate view.

Each bordereaux is mapped to the standard schema (risk id, inception/expiry, insured location, TIV, premium, commission, class). Rows failing schema mapping, with duplicate risk ids, or with premium/limit outside binder terms are quarantined before merge.

Consolidated premium and risk count reconcile to the sum of individual bordereaux control totals (delta = 0) and to the ledger premium booked for the binders; duplicates and rejects are quantified and excluded from the aggregate.

Consolidated bordereaux dataset and load log saved to /Delegated-Authority/Aggregate-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/bordereaux-consolidation/ as bdx_consolidated_v<n> with timestamp, source-file inventory and row counts; retained 7 years.

Mapping failures, duplicates and out-of-term rows logged in the bordereaux exception register with disposition (query coverholder / re-map / reject); recurring quality issues escalated to the Delegated Authority Manager and fed into coverholder scorecards.

checklist.step: Validate each bordereaux before merging
checklist.value: Schema mapping, duplicate detection and binder-term checks run on each file before it is admitted to the consolidated book.

testing.step: Reconcile consolidated totals to sources
testing.value: Consolidated premium and risk counts tie to the sum of source-bordereaux control totals with 0 variance.

checklist.step: Apply bordereaux domain data-quality rules
checklist.value: Required-field and format rules for the bordereaux domain quarantine non-conforming rows rather than loading them.

testing.step: Verify quarantine and disposition of bad rows
testing.value: 100% of quarantined rows carry a disposition and 0 duplicates persist in the consolidated dataset.

answers.value: Coordination with actuarial to feed delegated-authority results (earned premium, paid/incurred losses, aggregate exposure, rate movement by class) into IBNR reserving and pricing reviews; scope = the consolidated delegated book for the reserving/pricing cycle.
Provided to actuarial each quarter on the reserving cut-off (e.g. 2026-06-30), covering the delegated book's cumulative experience and the latest quarter's movement.

The actuarial data pack carries earned premium, paid and incurred losses, open case reserves, exposure and class mapping by coverholder and accident period. A pack with a premium/loss reconciliation break or missing class mapping is not released to actuarial.

Premium and loss totals reconcile to the consolidated bordereaux and to the ledger (delta = 0); triangulated experience ties to the prior submission plus the quarter's movement; any unreconciled coverholder is held back and noted.

Actuarial submission pack saved to /Delegated-Authority/Aggregate-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/actuarial-feed/ as delegated_actuarial_pack_v<n> with timestamp, data cut-off and reconciliation summary; retained 7 years and referenced in the reserving working papers.

Data gaps or reconciliation breaks logged in the exception register with disposition (correct / accrue estimate / flag as caveat to actuarial); material caveats communicated in writing to the Reserving Actuary alongside the pack.
The data-preparation methodology (earning basis, loss development mapping, class taxonomy) follows the approved delegated-reserving data standard version recorded in the reserving governance file.
Sensitivity: a >10% quarter-over-quarter movement in loss ratio for any material coverholder or class is flagged to actuarial for a documented reasonableness discussion before reserving relies on it.
Materiality: coverholders or classes above 10% of delegated premium, or whose experience moves the reserve indication materially, are separately reconciled and reviewed with the Reserving Actuary.
The full consolidated delegated book for the reserving period (census across coverholders and accident periods); every coverholder's premium and loss experience is reconciled before submission.

PASS = premium and losses reconcile to bordereaux and ledger, triangulation ties to the prior submission, and material caveats are documented. FAIL = an unreconciled coverholder, a triangulation break, or an undocumented data gap.

A reconciliation break is investigated and corrected, or an estimated accrual booked with a documented caveat to actuarial; open items tracked to closure within the reserving-cycle timetable (target 10 business days).
Acceptance = actuarial data pack reconciled to bordereaux and ledger, caveats documented, and the submission signed off by the Delegated Authority Manager and acknowledged by the Reserving Actuary.
Evidence (actuarial pack, reconciliation summary, caveat memo) stored in /Delegated-Authority/Aggregate-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/actuarial-feed/ and cross-referenced from the reserving working papers.

Approved methodology = the delegated-reserving data standard (earning basis, loss development mapping, class taxonomy) recorded in the reserving governance file; parameters sourced from the consolidated bordereaux and ledger, with the data cut-off and standard version logged on the submission.

checklist.step: Aggregate delegated experience for reserving
checklist.value: Premium, losses and exposure aggregated by coverholder and accident period and reconciled before hand-off to actuarial.

testing.step: Reconcile the actuarial feed to sources
testing.value: Premium and loss totals in the pack tie to bordereaux and ledger with 0 unexplained variance.

checklist.step: Validate the data feeding reserving
checklist.value: The actuarial pack passes completeness and reconciliation checks and known limitations are documented as caveats.

testing.step: Verify caveats and reconciliation are recorded
testing.value: 100% of material data gaps are documented as caveats and every material coverholder is reconciled.

checklist.step: Provide delegated results on the reserve-review timetable
checklist.value: The delegated data pack is delivered in time for the periodic reserve review with the agreed data cut-off.

testing.step: Confirm timely delivery each cycle
testing.value: The delegated actuarial feed is delivered by the reserving-cycle deadline for every period in the review with 0 misses.
